title: Lesson 46 - I Wish Things Were Different

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: You look as if you've rewritten that message several times.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: I have. I wish things were different. I want to help with the exhibition, but every extra request seems to arrive as an urgent favor.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: What do you wish were different exactly?

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: I wish community projects had a realistic design budget from the beginning. I also wish I had more free time this week.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Those wishes make sense, but what is the present reality?

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: The center hasn't confirmed a budget for the extra graphics, my client work is already scheduled, and the exhibition text still isn't final.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: So wishing doesn't mean that you can safely promise Friday.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: Right. If only the request were smaller and the wording were ready, I could assess it quickly. But neither condition is true.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: What part can you change?

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: I can't create more time or approve the center's budget, but I can make my current capacity clear.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: What would that look like in the reply?

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: The reality is that I can still make the original poster after the approved text and permissions arrive. I can't take on three additional graphics by Friday.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Can you offer anything that doesn't quietly expand the work?

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: What I can do is review a separate written brief next week. If there is a realistic deadline and budget, I can decide then.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: That sounds different from saying, “Maybe I'll squeeze it in.”

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: Much different. I wish I could say yes to every useful project, but I can only promise work that I have actually assessed.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Does your reply need to solve Priya's Friday problem?

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: No. I can acknowledge it and suggest that the center use an existing neutral template if it needs something before a new agreement.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Let's compare the options by honesty and workload. Which is the best fit?

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: Based on those criteria, the best fit is a clear no to Friday, plus an offer to review a separate brief next week. The downside is that Priya must find another short-term solution.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: And your actionable step?

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: Send the clarification today. My wishes explain how I feel; the message will explain what I can actually do.
